lessons: breakout logic must be separated from volatility/risk geometry and regime gating
ATR/volatility filters and costs can dominate apparent breakout profitability
runner/trailing/pyramiding must have explicit ownership and must not be evaluator-invented
mean reversion requires an explicit reverting/range regime and trend-transition invalidation
VWAP/deviation/RSI/Bollinger are feature proxies, not standalone alpha proof
natural targets may be equilibrium/inner bands but must be frozen and cost-tested
order-flow/depth/spread/adverse-selection features can be predictive but execution costs are part of the mechanism
maker/taker behavior can diverge during stress due to adverse selection
short-horizon strategies must prove expected move exceeds realistic spread/fee/slippage budget before economic replay
perpetual basis deviations arise under constrained arbitrage/speculative demand and may diminish over time
funding is a feedback mechanism and settlement/caps matter
OI is informative but exchange-level data quality can be inconsistent, requiring fail-closed source validation
periodicity/session effects require matched placebo controls and venue-portability checks
a paper-specific method must not be replaced by a coarse sign-only proxy
relative-value/arbitrage designs need explicit relationship stability, cost bounds and breakdown invalidation
terminal relative_value_psa history remains non-reactivatable by simple renaming
risk sizing must be tied to stop/risk distance rather than arbitrary fixed quantity
partial/trailing/runner/pyramiding ownership must be explicit and independently testable
